\section{Related Work}

-\paragraph{Training-free IE.} In-context learning for IE includes GPT-NER \cite{wang2023gptner}, which frames NER as sequence generation; UniNER \cite{zhou2023universalner}, which decomposes schemas into per-type queries; and GoLLIE \cite{sainz2023gollie}, which uses structured code generation. \paragraph{Schema complexity effects.} ``Lost in the Middle'' \cite{liu2024lost} demonstrates position-dependent degradation in long-context LLMs. We extend this line of analysis to the schema dimension: how the \emph{composition} of requested types---not just their count---determines extraction quality.
